response.answer: A protection-motivation-theory-based scale for DVT prophylaxis adherence was developed and validated for postdischarge hip/knee arthroplasty patients, focusing on medication adherence and self-efficacy. The scale underwent rigorous psychometric testing and mixed methods evaluation. It measures response efficacy and threat appraisal in healthcare measurement.

results.title: Patient compliance with deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis after total ...
results.content: Post-operative total joint patients are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE) and pulmonary embolisms (PE), and pharmacologic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis and/or mechanical compression devices have become the standard of care.[1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6589531/#ref1),[2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6589531/#ref2) Postoperative prophylaxis has demonstrated reduced complications associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and the benefits of prophylaxis have been demonstrated post discharge.[3-5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6589531/#ref3) Patient adherence to DVT prophylaxis has become even more critical given that the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) defines VTEs as never events, and Medicare will not cover the additional costs for managing these complications.[6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6589531/#ref6) To prevent VTEs, surgeons place arthroplasty patients on pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis postoperatively and discharge their patients with instructions to continue taking DVT prophylaxis medication for a total of 10 to
